content:
Apple will launch several new Mac products later this year, including the first MacBook with a touchscreen and the first models powered by the M6 chip. Here's everything we know so far about the upcoming Macs.

MacBook Ultra

The flagship Mac launching later this year will be Apple's first Mac to feature a touchscreen. Whether this new machine will ultimately be named MacBook Pro or MacBook Ultra remains undecided, but it will represent the most significant design overhaul of the MacBook Pro in years.

Reports indicate Apple is testing a high-end MacBook model running macOS 27.1, with an official launch expected at the end of October.

This new MacBook will be Apple's first laptop to feature both a touchscreen and an OLED display. The new machine is said to drop the notch design in favour of a Dynamic Island-style cutout similar to the iPhone. Bloomberg has also reported that the next-generation high-end MacBook will be thinner than the current MacBook Pro.

In terms of performance, the new touchscreen MacBook will continue to use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips found in the current MacBook Pro.

M6 MacBook

Reports suggest Apple plans to launch its first M6-powered Mac later this year, and is developing an updated entry-level MacBook Pro featuring the next-generation M6 processor.

Reports indicate the M6 will offer faster memory bandwidth, along with improvements in both CPU and GPU core performance.

Aside from the M6 chip, the new entry-level MacBook Pro is not expected to feature any other major changes.

iMac

Apple last updated the 24-inch iMac in October 2024, upgrading the chip from M3 to M4. Apple is currently working on the next-generation iMac update, reportedly set to launch this autumn.

The new iMac is expected to feature Apple's upcoming M6 chip. There are also rumours that the new iMac will be available in a range of fresh colour options.

Mac mini and Mac Studio (Potential Release)

Lastly, Apple is also developing updated versions of the Mac mini and Mac Studio, though specific launch dates remain unclear.

Reports indicate Apple is testing a new generation of Mac mini models equipped with M5 Pro and entry-level M6 chips, while the Mac Studio is being tested with M5 Max and M5 Ultra processors.

Bloomberg notes that the release dates for these models remain uncertain, depending on "memory chip supply." The market had previously widely expected the new Mac Studio to launch before year's end, but that now appears to be in question.

The current Mac mini offers M4 and M4 Pro chip options, while the Mac Studio is available with M4 Max and M3 Ultra configurations.

Summary

Affected by memory and storage supply constraints across the industry, Apple's current Mac lineup is in a somewhat awkward position. However, the company still has several highly competitive new machines ready to go. What are your thoughts on the new Macs launching before year's end? How much do you think the MacBook Ultra will be priced at? Let us know in the comments.
